spec_text:
# Game Specification: Treasure Grid

Build a playable browser game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
The game must run locally without external services or downloaded assets.

## Board

Display a 5 × 5 grid. Coordinates are (row, column), starting at (1, 1)
in the top-left corner.

Initial positions:
- Player: (1, 1)
- Treasures: (1, 5), (3, 3), and (5, 1)
- Walls: (2, 2), (2, 3), and (4, 4)
- Trap: (3, 5)
- Exit: (5, 5)

Use distinct visual appearances for each type of cell.

## Controls

- Arrow keys move the player one cell per key press.
- Moving outside the board or into a wall has no effect.
- Arrow keys must not scroll the page.

## Rules

- The score starts at 0.
- Collecting a treasure increases the score by 1 and removes that treasure.
- Each treasure can be collected only once.
- Reaching the exit before collecting all three treasures does not end the game.
- Reaching the exit after collecting all three treasures wins the game.
- Entering the trap immediately loses the game.
- After winning or losing, movement is disabled.

## Interface

- Display the board, score, controls, and current game status.
- The initial status is "Playing".
- On victory, display "You Win!".
- On defeat, display "Game Over".
- Provide a visible "Restart" button at all times.
- Restart must restore every initial position, all treasures, score 0,
  and status "Playing".

## Delivery

Include a README with exact instructions for starting and playing the game.

criteria.description: Documented launch command starts the game, the play surface becomes reachable, and the process is shut down cleanly after the check.
Core gameplay rules from the specification are observable while running: # Game Specification: Treasure Grid Build a playable browser game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Player input changes game state (keyboard/pointer). Opening a page without an observable state change does not pass.
Technical constraints: runs with local/programmatic assets as required.

Test contract: expose window.__gameState with the REAL live game state (grid: {cols: 5, rows: 5} board dimensions in cells; player: {col, row} player position in grid units, (1,1) top-left; score: number, current score (treasures collected); status: 'playing' | 'won' | 'lost'; treasuresRemaining: number, how many of the 3 treasures are still on the board) and window.__gameTest setup hooks (placePlayer: placePlayer(col, row): teleport the player to an open floor cell, keep playing; collectAllTreasures: collectAllTreasures(): remove all 3 treasures and set score to 3, keep playing). Hooks only set preconditions and must use the real game logic; they never fake results.
ArrowRight moves the player one cell to the right [test: saved.c0 = s.player.col; key ArrowRight; wait 100; expect s.player.col === saved.c0 + 1 && s.player.row === 1; expect s.status === 'playing']
Moving outside the board has no effect [test: saved.c0 = s.player.col; saved.r0 = s.player.row; key ArrowUp; key ArrowLeft; wait 100; expect s.player.col === saved.c0 && s.player.row === saved.r0]

Moving into a wall has no effect (wall at row 2, col 2) [test: key ArrowDown; wait 100; saved.c0 = s.player.col; saved.r0 = s.player.row; key ArrowRight; wait 100; expect s.player.col === saved.c0 && s.player.row === saved.r0]

Collecting a treasure increases the score by 1 and removes it [test: __gameTest.placePlayer(4, 1); key ArrowRight; wait 100; expect s.player.col === 5 && s.player.row === 1; expect s.score === 1; expect s.treasuresRemaining === 2; expect s.status === 'playing']

Entering the trap at (row 3, col 5) immediately loses the game [test: __gameTest.placePlayer(5, 2); key ArrowDown; wait 100; expect s.player.col === 5 && s.player.row === 3; expect s.status === 'lost']

Reaching the exit before collecting all three treasures does not end the game [test: __gameTest.placePlayer(5, 4); key ArrowDown; wait 100; expect s.player.col === 5 && s.player.row === 5; expect s.status === 'playing']

Reaching the exit after collecting all three treasures wins the game [test: __gameTest.collectAllTreasures(); __gameTest.placePlayer(5, 4); key ArrowDown; wait 100; expect s.player.col === 5 && s.player.row === 5; expect s.status === 'won']

Movement is disabled after losing [test: __gameTest.placePlayer(5, 2); key ArrowDown; wait 100; saved.c0 = s.player.col; saved.r0 = s.player.row; key ArrowLeft; key ArrowUp; wait 100; expect s.player.col === saved.c0 && s.player.row === saved.r0; expect s.status === 'lost']

The visible Restart button (#restart) restores initial positions, treasures, score 0 and status playing [test: __gameTest.placePlayer(4, 1); key ArrowRight; wait 100; expect s.score === 1; click #restart; wait 100; expect s.score === 0; expect s.player.col === 1 && s.player.row === 1; expect s.treasuresRemaining === 3; expect s.status === 'playing']
Arrow keys must not scroll the page [test: key ArrowDown x3; wait 100; expect window.scrollY === 0 && window.scrollX === 0]
Informational only, nothing to implement: 10 spec-derived requirements

tasks.description: Create game/index.html with inline <style>: page layout, 5x5 grid rendered as HTML5 <canvas>, distinct colors for player, treasures, walls, trap, exit, floor; visible DOM elements for title, Score, Status, controls help, and a Restart button with id 'restart'. Include keyboard handler on window with preventDefault for arrow keys to avoid page scrolling.

Implement core game logic in game/game.js: initial state (player (1,1), treasures (1,5),(3,3),(5,1), walls (2,2),(2,3),(4,4), trap (3,5), exit (5,5)), arrow-key movement blocked by board edges and walls, treasure collection (+1 score, remove treasure), trap = immediate loss, exit wins only after all 3 treasures, movement disabled after win/loss.

Implement rendering and UI updates: draw board on canvas each state change, update DOM text Score and Status ('Playing', 'You Win!', 'Game Over'), and Restart button handler restoring full initial state (positions, all treasures, score 0, status playing).

Implement test contract: expose window.__gameState as a live getter returning {grid:{cols:5,rows:5}, player:{col,row}, score, status:'playing'|'won'|'lost', treasuresRemaining} and window.__gameTest with placePlayer(col,row) and collectAllTreasures() that set preconditions through the real game logic.

Verify launch path and no-asset constraints: confirm game runs with 'python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1' from game/, all files local, no CDN/build step, no runtime errors, keyboard works without clicking.
Write game/README.md with exact launch instructions (python3 -m http.server 8000 from game/, open http://127.0.0.1:8000/) and how to play (arrow keys, goal, trap, restart).
